name: DM Control reacher easy feedback policy
summary: DM Control reacher easy feedback policy. Bounded native-control simulation with privileged state; not a trained policy or hardware deployment.

license.scope: Pinned upstream Apache-2.0 source; preserve notices and model/asset terms. Hub feedback adapter is MIT.

observation.description: Privileged simulator state and declared goals; no perception or real sensor validation.

hardware: Linux x86_64; CPU simulation; see retained receipt for the exact host environment
requirements.rendering: Headless. EGL libraries are required for MuJoCo imports; PushT uses SDL dummy video. No interactive display.
requirements.dependency_lock: Direct runtime versions are pinned and measured. The receipt retains the complete environment freeze; prepare records the installed environment. System drivers are separate host requirements.

invocation.example: Prepare explicitly; run --example or replace it with --input TASK.json. --describe reads the bounded contract without running simulation.

conventions.coordinate_frame: Native pinned DM Control model world frame; no external frame conversion

preconditions: Use the exact recorded source, Linux Python 3.10 environment and pinned direct packages.
No physical robot, network actuation or external robot credentials.
postconditions: All reported checks must be true and all output numbers finite.
Success covers the declared goal and frozen cases, not arbitrary tasks or physical hardware.

completion.success_condition: All declared goal and finite-state checks pass; exit 0 with task_complete. Mean native task reward over the final 100 control steps >= 0.9 with finite state and nonzero control. Episode rewards are not task-agnostic accuracy.
failure_modes: Goal not reached within bounded steps
completion.stop_condition: Terminate the adapter at the recorded timeout. No physical hardware is opened.

evidence.result: All 3 frozen cases completed against this exact adapter and source.

contribution.instructions: Change the runtime expansion manifest/template, regenerate, and rerun all frozen cases. Preserve source/model/checkpoint licenses and distinguish simulation from hardware.
